rv.q: Raúf’s story acts like a much-needed empathy machine for a country that is in danger of losing its moral compass.
The result of this was an incredibly striking piece of theatre.
This is a genuinely touching piece of theatre, and with a government hell-bent on demonising refugees, is exactly the kind of story we need to be sharing with younger audiences.
The Boy at the Back of the Class is an energetic, emotive and imaginative adaptation that deserves to be seen by all ages.
Director Monique Touko writes in the show’s programme that she wanted to create the show she wished she saw as a child, and frankly, my wish would be that every child could see this show.
